Setit to zero to find critical points: PR 3. Check each critical point to determine which corresponds to a minimum (and which might be a maximum or inflection point). 4. Compare function values at these critical points (and potentially at boundaries, if any) to identify the global minimum. This approach shows the basic calculus idea: you look for where the slope is zero and then see which point gives the smallest value of the function.
